answer: A practical sybil defense is to require each agent to post a refundable stake before it can place orders, then slash that stake when a fraud proof shows it double-spent or broke a market rule. Creating many identities no longer grants free influence: each must lock scarce capital, and detected cheating destroys part of it. A wharf may route trade through a karst-shaped delta of local markets, but the same stake rule applies in every branch.
